system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
The Seller’s “STANDARD”, “FINAL” and alleged prior-agreement labels are not evidence of Buyer approval. The positions below are Buyer negotiation proposals, based on the supplied extracts—not verification of the underlying DD documents. The baseline remains **AUD 24 million for 100% of Paperbark, debt-free/cash-free, under NSW law**.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 General liability cap** | General warranty liability capped at 20%: **AUD 4.8m**. | Meaningful recovery for general warranties, with separate protection for fundamental warranties, tax and specific risks. | **Counter with 50% (AUD 12m), subject to DD and recovery security;** the Seller has not substantiated its market assertion or shown that AUD 4.8m adequately protects Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-002 De minimis & basket** | Claims must exceed **AUD 25,000**; **AUD 250,000 deductible basket**, recovering only the excess. | Lower thresholds, a tipping basket, aggregation of related claims and exclusions for special claim categories. | **Propose AUD 10,000 de minimis and AUD 120,000 tipping basket;** the current combination leaves Buyer bearing substantial losses before meaningful recovery. |
| **SPA-N-003 General claims time limit** | Notice within **18 months**; limitations extend to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | At least **24 months** for general warranties; timely notified claims preserved, including reasonably described contingent claims. | **Counter at 24 months and restrict this deadline to general warranties;** Buyer needs adequate post-Completion reporting cycles to identify problems. |
| **SPA-N-004 Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title subject to the general cap and time limits. | Separate title, capacity and authority warranties; no thresholds, purchase-price cap at minimum and longer survival. | **Require a separate regime—at least AUD 24m cap and six-year contractual notification period, checked against execution form and applicable law;** defective ownership should not receive ordinary business-warranty treatment. |
| **SPA-N-005 Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance apply to all Claims; no express fraud exception supplied. | Express preservation of fraud and fraudulent misrepresentation claims, including relevant attribution to Seller representatives. | **Carve fraud out of caps, thresholds, contractual time bars, disclosure/knowledge defences and remedy/reliance restrictions, preserving non-excludable rights;** blanket wording must not purport to shelter fraudulent conduct. |
| **SPA-N-006 Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the data room, referenced material, accounts, registers and public records. | Only fair disclosure with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the relevant matter; a frozen, indexed disclosure record. | **Reject blanket deemed disclosure and require specific, intelligible disclosures against relevant warranties;** document availability is not adequate notice of a risk, and disclosure must not defeat specific indemnities or Completion obligations. |
| **SPA-N-007 Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known by Buyer or advisers, including anything discoverable from records. | Delete the qualifier; fallback limited to actual conscious knowledge of named Buyer personnel, without imputation or investigation duty. | **Reject constructive and adviser-imputed knowledge;** Buyer’s diligence should not transfer undiscovered or poorly disclosed risks back to Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-008 Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied by delivery of written consent. No final consent or evidence of satisfaction of associated conditions supplied. | A Buyer-benefit condition requiring effective consent and satisfaction of clause 11.3 conditions, without unacceptable contract changes. | **Require satisfaction before Completion, with waiver solely at Buyer’s election and a longstop/termination right;** approximately 30% of FY26 revenue depends on this relationship. |
| **SPA-N-009 Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** outstanding; security release after Completion. | Verified payout figures, repayment through Completion funds flow and effective contemporaneous releases of security and relevant guarantees. | **Make discharge a Completion requirement, supported by binding lender arrangements and subsequent registration evidence;** Buyer must not inherit funded debt or secured assets contrary to the debt-free bargain. |
| **SPA-N-010 Employee bonuses** | **AUD 420,000** conditional bonuses are a Seller matter but omitted from funds flow; on-costs unspecified. | Seller economic responsibility for transaction bonuses and applicable payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs, with payment and withholding mechanics. | **Quantify and include them as Seller-funded payments or a defined debt-like deduction, backed by an indemnity and no double counting;** omission could leave Buyer funding transaction-triggered liabilities after Completion. |
| **SPA-N-011 Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; **AUD 180,000** recorded open and transfer conditional on cleared payment. | Verified cleared payment and effective assignment of relevant IP; protection for ownership defects, third-party claims and remediation costs. | **Require payment/assignment evidence at Completion and broaden the specific indemnity beyond the invoice amount, outside general limitations;** an open ledger is not conclusive proof of non-payment, but ownership remains unverified. |
| **SPA-N-012 Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary operational matter, said unlikely to be material; access, scope and notification obligations unresolved. | Prompt investigation, evidence preservation, containment and legal assessment of notification duties; protection for pre-Completion incident liabilities. | **Require investigation/remediation covenants and a tailored indemnity for resulting costs and legally recoverable liabilities;** neither a confirmed notifiable breach nor immateriality is established. |
| **SPA-N-013 Sandbar renewals** | Three **AUD 110,000** renewals treated as ordinary-course costs. | Combined review of **AUD 330,000**, including execution dates, service periods, cancellation rights, accruals and ordinary-course status. | **Reserve treatment pending DD: allocate through working capital, debt-like adjustments or specific protection as appropriate;** neither ordinary-course treatment nor automatic deduction is justified on the supplied facts. |
| **SPA-N-014 Category separation** | General limitations and exclusive-remedy/non-reliance terms potentially govern every Claim. | Expressly separate general warranties, fundamentals, tax, specific indemnities, price adjustments, debt discharge, covenants and fraud. | **Add a claims-regime matrix and express precedence/carve-outs throughout the SPA;** broad cross-references could otherwise neutralise negotiated protections. |
| **SPA-N-015 Title verification** | DD-012 share register records Harbourglass as holding 100%. | Verification of issued capital, ownership chain, encumbrances, options/convertibles and transfer restrictions, plus effective transfer and registration deliverables. | **Verify title independently and retain full title warranties and Completion deliverables;** the register is relevant evidence, not complete assurance of unencumbered ownership of all issued shares. |
| **SPA-N-016 Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP warranties treated as settled under the general regime. | Separate pre-Completion tax indemnity and tax warranties with suitable caps and survival; robust IP ownership, licensing, infringement and contractor-assignment protection. | **Keep both open: negotiate tax survival through applicable assessment/reassessment periods plus a buffer, and risk-based IP limits alongside Ironquay protection;** an 18-month/20% general regime may expire too soon or underprotect core liabilities and assets. |

**Avoid overreaching on consent requirements:** the supplied office lease material identifies a **notification** obligation, not landlord consent; Mossvale’s **assignment** restriction does not itself establish a consent requirement for this share sale. Check the full contracts before imposing either as a consent condition.
=== END ADVICE ===
